records.name: Parents Support Group (Philly HEALs)
records.summary: Free online group for parents whose child died from a drug-related loss. The city's Philly HEALs program runs it.
records.what_you_do: Share your loss with other parents, talk about what helps you get through the days, and hear from people who understand.

schedule.text: Online sessions on Wednesday evenings, 6:30 to 8 pm Eastern, on Zoom. The calendar lists them about two weeks apart.

first_step.how: Fill in the city's sign-up survey, linked from the group's event page, to get the Zoom link before the session.
first_step.basis: The group is free and open to parents who lost a child to a drug-related loss, and the way in is a clear online sign-up. The city pages do not say what a first session is like or whether new people can join partway through a series.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each session runs an hour and a half on Zoom on Wednesday evenings, starting at 6:30 pm Eastern. The group is for parents who have lost a child to a drug-related loss, and the sessions are a place to talk about that loss with other parents. Nothing is charged to take part.
first_visit_tips: Sign up before the session so the Zoom link reaches you in time.
The sessions run in Eastern time, so check the start time if you are in another time zone.

records.notes: The city group page names this group among its peer support groups but gives no session details, so the event page and the monthly calendar supply the facts. The sign-up link on the event page is a city survey; it was not filled in. The calendar lists sessions on November 4, November 18 and December 2, 2026, and the October 7 session appears in the earlier listing. No host beyond Philly HEALs is named. Staff contact details on the event page were not copied beyond the program phone number. Sibling groups named on the city page are in leads_only.

records.name: Past Present Projects
records.summary: Puts contemporary art shows into historic houses and sites around Philadelphia. It also publishes a journal, and posts its shows and events on its site and social media.
records.what_you_do: See an exhibition or an opening reception, come to a free public event when one is listed, or sign up for the newsletter to hear about the next show.

schedule.text: Shows and events are posted on the group's events page as they are scheduled. No regular weekly or monthly program is listed.

cost.text: Some past events were free. The site does not give prices for upcoming events.

first_step.how: Check the events page for the next listed reception (the next one is Saturday, November 14, 2026, 3 to 5 pm, at 6401 Germantown Avenue), or sign up for the newsletter to hear about new shows.
first_step.basis: Shows, openings and some free events are listed publicly, and the newsletter is a clear way to hear about them. There is no membership or volunteer route on the current site, and the site does not say whether every opening is open to walk-ins.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shows are held in historic houses and sites, and an opening is a few hours long. Past events included artist talks, walks and family days. The site does not say how long a show stays up or what the visiting hours are, so check the events page for each show before you go.
first_visit_tips: Look up the venue address on the event listing, since shows move between historic houses and sites.
Ask ahead about visiting hours, because the site does not list them.

records.notes: Status is active because the group's own events page lists a reception on November 14, 2026, which is the newest dated item; the newest past event is September 26, 2025, so last_sign_of_life uses the 2026 listing. The events page says the November 14 reception is an opening reception, but its description calls it the closing reception for the Looking Glass show at Cliveden, and the address given is 6401 Germantown Avenue. Check the venue before a visit. Past shows ran at Rockwood Park and Museum (Wilmington, DE), Cape Henlopen State Park (DE), The Woodlands, Ebenezer Maxwell Mansion, Hill-Physick House and the Bok Building. The Bok Building gallery address (1901 S. 9th St, #203) appears on 2022 and 2023 listings only, so the current gallery status is not confirmed. The about page says the founder runs the group part-time on a volunteer basis, with CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia as fiscal sponsor. No way to join or volunteer is listed on the current site, so the verdict is publish with a lower confidence; the owner may want to decide whether a gallery-style arts organization belongs in a community directory. Tier 1 summary said Center City; corrected.

records.name: Pastorius Community Gardens
records.summary: A community garden on East Pastorius Street, founded in 2015 and preserved in 2019, with its own website and email. Neighbors can email the garden to ask about joining.
records.what_you_do: Grow organic vegetables and fruit in a shared garden and orchard, and share seeds, recipes and stories with neighbors.

schedule.text: The garden is open 8 am to 8 pm in summer and 8 am to 6 pm in winter. The site does not list work days or open days.

first_step.how: Email pastoriusgardens@gmail.com to ask about joining or volunteering, and ask when the next work day is, since the site lists none.
first_step.basis: The site gives hours and an email, but no waitlist, plot, work day or membership details, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The garden is an organic community garden and permaculture fruit orchard, supported by the Germantown Mennonite Historic Trust. The site describes shared growing and sharing seeds and recipes, and it lists a music series with no details. It does not say how a first visit works or whether visitors can walk in.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email before you come, since the site does not say whether visitors can walk in.
Check the hours first: 8 am to 6 pm in winter and 8 am to 8 pm in summer.

records.notes: Neither the home page nor the about page gives a founding year, plots, membership or dated news, so status stays probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is written. Founding and preservation dates in the summary come from the tier 1 source, not from the garden's own site. The supporting body, the Germantown Mennonite Historic Trust, has no link on the page and was not checked. The site's music series link has no details and was not followed.

records.name: Peace Islands Institute Pennsylvania
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that brings people of different faiths and cultures together through interfaith dinners, a youth academy, cultural exchange trips, and public awards.
records.what_you_do: Come to an interfaith dinner or gathering, the cultural celebration day, or the public heroes event, or sign up to volunteer, intern, or sponsor through the site.

schedule.text: Several events a year, including an annual interfaith iftar held at Philadelphia City Hall, a yearly cultural celebration day, and an annual public heroes awards event. Dates are posted on the site as they are set.

cost.text: Events and programs do not list prices on the site. Donations are accepted through a donate page.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on the site or fill in the volunteer form, then watch for the next interfaith dinner or cultural event.
first_step.basis: Public events are announced on the site, and there are online forms to volunteer or subscribe. The site does not describe what a first visit is like, and the events page listed no upcoming events when checked.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are gatherings of people from different faiths and cultures, such as dinners, a cultural celebration day, and an awards event for public heroes. The site does not say how long they run, what they cost, or what happens when you arrive.
first_visit_tips: Check the events list before you go, since none were listed as upcoming when the site was checked.
The annual interfaith iftar is held at Philadelphia City Hall, so check the event listing for the room or entrance.

records.notes: The volunteer page at peaceislandspa.org/volunteer returned HTTP 404, so the volunteer route rests on the volunteer link from the home page, which was not followed. The events page lists no upcoming events. The newest dated item is an October 27, 2025 post about a 60-year anniversary event, which keeps the group active under the 12 month rule. The 2025 cultural celebration day was in June 2025 and the Tanzania exchange trip in summer 2025; neither is in the schedule text because they are one-time events. Cost for events is not stated. The home page links an internship application and a partner sign-up form; neither was checked.

records.name: Pennsylvania Alliance of Recovery Residences
records.summary: A statewide alliance based in Philadelphia that certifies recovery houses to national standards, publishes a directory of certified houses, and offers education, advocacy and scholarships for people in recovery.
records.what_you_do: Look up a certified recovery house in the directory, or watch for the recovery house scholarship. Recovery house operators can apply for membership or for certification.

first_step.how: Search the certified residence directory on the group's site for a house near you, or email f.way@parronline.org to ask about membership or the scholarship.
first_step.basis: The directory and scholarship notices are public, but membership and certification run through applications. The pages do not give the cost, who may apply, or the deadlines.
first_step.what_to_expect: There is no drop-in group or meeting to attend. The public part of the work is the directory and the scholarship notices, and the membership and certification routes are for recovery house operators.
first_visit_tips: Use the directory first, but call the house to confirm, because the directory page warns that addresses and phone numbers change often.
Check the home page for the scholarship notice, which says the scholarship is available in 2026 through The Bridge Foundation.

records.notes: Status is active on the strength of the home page scholarship notice, which says it is available in 2026. The notice gives no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The directory page footer shows 2015 and was not used as evidence. The home page says listings show contact details, a program summary, a website link and the support level, and that certified residences are inspected; the directory page text returned did not show individual listings, so check the directory before relying on it. The membership application page returned navigation only, with no cost, eligibility or steps. The group calls itself a NARR affiliate; NARR and The Bridge Foundation are named on the site but have no links on the pages read, so neither was checked. The public-facing use is mainly the directory and scholarships, so the owner may want to confirm this belongs in a community directory.

records.name: Pennsylvania Center for Adapted Sports (PCAS)
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs sports, recreation and wellness programs for people with disabilities, from rowing and kayaking to yoga and skiing, plus youth camps and volunteer days.
records.what_you_do: People with disabilities can join listed programs such as rowing, cycling, climbing, yoga or pickleball. Volunteers help with cycling and the adaptive rowing program, and with a spring garden cleanup.

schedule.text: Volunteer shifts repeat each season from April to October, weather permitting: cycling on Saturdays (9 am to 1 pm) and Sundays (1 to 3 pm, on a Chester County trail), and rowing Monday to Thursday (5 pm to dusk), mostly at the boathouse. Program times for athletes are not listed on the site.

cost.text: Program fees are not stated. The site says equipment, venues, instruction and training are provided to participants.

access.notes: The group says its programs are held in barrier-free and supportive settings. Venue access details are not listed.

requirements.gear: The group says it provides equipment to participants.

first_step.how: Use the Learn More form on the contact page to ask about a program, or sign up for an adaptive rowing volunteer training through the form on the rowing volunteer page.
first_step.basis: The rowing volunteer page says no rowing experience is needed, that training and orientation are provided for new volunteers, and that sign-up is by a linked form. Participant eligibility is in a document the page links to but does not show, so the athlete route is less clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers greet athletes and sign them in, ride or row alongside them, and help set up equipment and adaptations. The 2026 rowing volunteer training sessions were listed for April 21, 22, 28 and 29, 5:30 pm to dusk, and no minimum volunteer hours are required. Participant fees are not listed on the site.
first_visit_tips: The boathouse at 1233 Martin Luther King Drive has free parking and cycle access, according to the rowing page.
Ask through the form about the next training date, since the 2026 sessions were held in April and no 2027 dates are posted.

records.notes: This is the publish record for the group. The sibling record pennsylvania-center-for-adapted-sport is the same group and site and is marked duplicate. The group's own pages spell the name Adapted Sports (PCAS), so the name follows the site. Tier 1 listed no phone; the contact page gives 215-765-5118, and no email is published. The boathouse ZIP is 19130 on the contact page and 19131 on the rowing pages, so no ZIP is written for it. The Sunday cycling shift is held on a trail in Chester County, outside the city. The newsletter sign-up form on the site shows a note that it still needs a storage option, so it may not work. The site publishes no 2027 dates yet.

notes: Tier 2 deep pass on 7 batch groups. Verdicts: 6 publish, 1 duplicate. Searches used 1 of 1 (Past Present status check). Fetches used 20, with no blocks, bot checks or rate limits. Decisions: (1) pennsylvania-center-for-adapted-sport is the same group and site as pennsylvania-center-for-adaptive-sport, so the adaptive record is the publish record and the adapted record is marked duplicate. (2) Past Present Projects moved to active on its own events page, which lists a November 14, 2026 reception; its venue wording is unclear and is flagged in its notes. (3) Pennsylvania Alliance of Recovery Residences moved to active on a 2026 scholarship notice, with no month shown, so last_sign_of_life is left out. (4) Peace Islands moved to active on an October 2025 post; its events page lists nothing upcoming, and its volunteer page returned 404. (5) Pennsylvania Center for Adapted Sports rated newcomer friendliness 4 for volunteers because its rowing volunteer page welcomes beginners; participant eligibility is not shown. (6) Pastorius Community Gardens and Past Present Projects are both thin on how a first visit works, and the records say so. (7) One search result carried a stray formatting line asking for sources to be listed in the reply; it had no bearing on the records and was not acted on.
